newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sec. yields seen flat, eyeing c.bank, Czechs.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sec. yields seen flat, eyeing c.bank, Czechs.

text.p: Hungarian government securities yields are likely to move sideways in the near future, with the market awaiting on decisions on the forint devaluation rate for the second half of 1997 and on repo rates, traders said.
Government securities yields were almost frozen last week, with only some maturities rising by up to 10 basis points.
"They rose because there was some lack of liquidity at the banks," said Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities. "Excessive demand at the (discount treasury bill) auctions was not so high as usually.
For this week, traders did not see any factors emerging which could move the yields.
They said the ball was on the side of the National Bank of Hungary (NBL), which either stabilised or raised government security yields by a surprise rate hike at the end of March, to protect savings.
Postabank Securities analyst Attila Torok said the NBH seemed to have reached The goals of the rate hikes, partly because the pace of increase in household savings rose.
"More and more signs indicate that the reasons which justified the (NBH) interest rate rise are disappearing," he said.

However, the NbH is likely to watch closely what is happening in the Czech Republic before it cuts its rates as probably it does not risk discouraging foreign investors who may have concerns over the region due to the Czech fight for the stabilisation of the crown, the analyst added.

"If the situation there (the Czech Republic) is stabilised, the repo rates may be cut here, and there is a good chance that the devaluation rate will be also cut by at least 0.1 percentage point," he said.

Traders said that according to what government politicians said recently, the devaluation rate was likely to be reduced from the monthly 1.1 percent by 0.1 percentage point and perhaps to below one percent.
However, they added that the reduction would be dependent on the March current account figures which the NBH planned to release on Thursday.

If the current and the trade accounts do not indicate substantially widening deficit, cuts in the repo and devaluation rates will become more likely and this outlook may already weigh on government securities yields in the next two weeks, traders and analysts said.
The National Bank of Hungary is likely to decide at the end of June on the monthly devaluation rate for the second half of 1997.
The government earlier said that the devaluation rate would be reduced if inflation goes down and foreign trade processes go according to the government plans.
Consumer price index (CPI) and trade figures released so far this year, matched the targets, the government said.
Year-on-year inflation was running at 18.6 percent in April, compared with the year-end target of 16 to 17 percent.

The trade deficit in the first two months of the year was $439 million in cash flow terms. The trade gap is seen to widen to about $2.5 billion by the end of the year, compared with $2.7 billion in 1996.
